title: Orbital Momentum Transfer Lab
description: A flamingo stands on a rotating platform at the center of the scene, while a DamagedHelmet orbits it like a satellite. The user manipulates orbital radius, angular velocity, and platform spin to explore conservation of angular momentum, transferring momentum between the helmet and the flamingo's platform through coupled controls, with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load flamingo.glb and place it standing upright at the origin on a visible circular platform (flat cyan cylinder, radius 2). Load DamagedHelmet.glb and place it orbiting the flamingo in a circular orbit on the XZ plane. Implement a physics simulation of angular momentum conservation: the system has total angular momentum L = I_platform * omega_platform + m_helmet * r^2 * omega_orbit, which must remain constant. UI panel (HTML overlay, top-left) with: (1) a slider for orbit radius r (range 3-12), which auto-adjusts omega_orbit to conserve L; (2) a slider for helmet orbital speed omega_orbit, which auto-adjusts platform spin omega_platform to conserve L; (3) a button to apply an impulse torque (+/- delta L) to the helmet, changing total system L and visibly speeding/slowing both objects; (4) a 'Transfer Momentum' button that shifts angular momentum from orbit to platform spin or vice versa over 2 seconds with smooth animation; (5) Undo and Redo buttons that restore previous states of all parameters (store at least 20 states, push state on every slider release, button press). Display real-time readouts: L_total, omega_platform, omega_orbit, r, kinetic energy of each subsystem. The flamingo platform rotates around Y-axis at omega_platform; the helmet orbits at omega_orbit, always facing the flamingo (lookAt). Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,10,18) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: ambient light (0.4) plus one directional light from (5,10,7) with shadows enabled on a ground plane. Draw a dashed ring (THREE.RingGeometry or Line) showing the current orbit path. Animate with requestAnimationFrame, updating positions each frame based on current angular velocities. The task requires at least 10 interactions: adjust radius twice, adjust speed twice, apply impulse twice, transfer momentum twice, undo once, redo once.
